title: PCI-DSS cardholder data scope
why: Card data changes the architecture, not just the rigor: the cheapest compliant design is one where the card number never reaches the application at all. That decision belongs in the packet, before a form is built.

addRequirements.title: Card data never reaches application storage
addRequirements.statement: The application shall keep every full card number and security code outside its own storage, logs and request bodies by using provider-hosted fields or tokens.
addRequirements.definition: Scope stays small because the card number is never available to the {secondary}'s own servers.
addRequirements.failurePath: If a request carries a card-shaped value, it is rejected and logged as a redaction event, not stored.
acceptance: Given a request body containing a 16-digit card number, when it is processed, then it is refused and the value is absent from logs.
Given the storage schema, when it is inspected, then it contains no field that holds a full card number or a security code.

addRequirements.title: Tokens are the only reference to a payment instrument
addRequirements.statement: When the application refers to a payment method, the application shall use a provider-issued token bound to one customer and one tenant.
addRequirements.definition: A leaked token cannot be moved to another customer or tenant without the provider rejecting it.
addRequirements.failurePath: If a token belongs to another tenant, the operation is refused and reported rather than attempted.
acceptance: Given a token issued for tenant A, when tenant B presents it, then the operation is refused.
Given a stored reference, when it is read, then it is a token, never a card fragment.

addRequirements.title: Production changes require separation of duties
addRequirements.statement: The build pipeline shall refuse a production-affecting change whose approver is also its author.
addRequirements.definition: No single identity can move unreviewed code into the environment that touches money.
addRequirements.failurePath: If the approval record is missing, the change is refused rather than treated as implicitly approved.
acceptance: Given a change approved by its author, when CI evaluates it, then it is refused.
Given an approved change, when the record is read, then it names the reviewer and the revision.

addGates.statement: No request body, schema field or log line can hold a full card number, proven by a test.
